NGA.note: FAOSTAT 2024: Nigeria is the world's #1 producer of roots & tubers — cassava ~57-60 Mt (18% of global cassava) plus ~50 Mt of yam (over 70% of world yam output). Combined roots ~113 Mt, but more than 90% is processed into gari/fufu/flour and eaten domestically; HS0714 trade is negligible. The clearest case of production hugely exceeding trade — roots are eaten where grown, a core food-security staple for Sub-Saharan Africa.

COD.note: FAOSTAT 2024: DR Congo is the world's #2 cassava producer (~14% of global output, ~48 Mt). Cassava is the dietary staple — almost entirely consumed domestically as fresh roots, chikwangue and flour. Trade in HS0714 is minimal; production vastly exceeds any trade.

GHA.note: FAOSTAT 2024: Ghana is a top-5 cassava producer (~8% of global cassava, ~27 Mt) plus large yam output (~9 Mt) and cocoyam; combined roots ~50 Mt. Mostly domestic (fufu, gari, kokonte); small fresh-cassava and yam exports to the UK/diaspora markets (HS0714). Production far exceeds trade.

THA.note: FAOSTAT/USDA 2024: Thailand produces ~30 Mt of cassava and is the world's #1 cassava EXPORTER (~60-65% of world cassava trade), shipping chips/pellets and starch to China. It also IMPORTS large volumes of fresh roots from Laos, Cambodia and Myanmar to feed its starch/chip processors, then re-exports. The exp figure here spans HS0714 chips plus the starch (HS1108) chain the country is built around; HS0714-only fresh+dried trade is the ~2 Mt THA->CHN flow.

VNM.note: FAOSTAT/Vietnam Customs 2024: Vietnam produces ~10.5 Mt cassava and is the world's #3 cassava exporter — China takes ~93% by volume. Total cassava-and-products exports ~2.43 Mt in 2024; the HS0714 fresh+dried-chips portion (VNM->CHN ~422 kt) sits alongside a larger cassava-starch (HS1108) trade. Net exporter.

KHM.note: FAOSTAT 2024: Cambodia (#7 cassava producer) grows ~13 Mt and exports most of it — primarily fresh/dried roots and chips across the border to Thailand's processors (KHM->THA ~2,076 kt HS0714) plus growing starch shipments to China/Vietnam. Cambodia supplies ~31% of Thailand's cassava imports. Strong net exporter.

LAO.note: FAOSTAT/Lao trade portal 2024: Laos is now Thailand's single largest cassava supplier — ~68% of Thai cassava imports (LAO->THA ~2,415 kt, the biggest flow in the dataset). Xayaboury province alone produced ~1.56 Mt in 2024. Almost all output is exported fresh/dried; little domestic processing. Heavy net exporter.

IDN.note: FAOSTAT 2024: Indonesia is the #4-6 cassava producer (~19-20 Mt) plus sweet potato. Cassava is a domestic staple and starch feedstock; trade is small relative to output and Indonesia is a modest net importer of cassava starch/chips in some years. Production hugely exceeds HS0714 trade.

BRA.note: FAOSTAT 2024: Brazil produces ~18-23 Mt of cassava (mandioca), the staple of the north/northeast eaten as farinha and used for tapioca starch. Almost entirely domestic; HS0714 trade negligible. Production dwarfs trade.

CHN.note: FAOSTAT/China Customs 2024: China is the world's #1 sweet-potato producer (>50 Mt, ~55% of global) — mostly domestic food/feed/alcohol. It is also the world's #1 cassava IMPORTER, buying ~8 Mt of cassava products a year (chips/pellets for animal feed and ethanol, plus starch) from Thailand, Vietnam, Laos and Cambodia. The imp figure spans the HS0714 chip trade plus the cassava-starch (HS1108) demand the import market is built on. Large net importer of cassava.

TZA.note: FAOSTAT 2024: Tanzania is a top-10 cassava producer (~8 Mt) and growing sweet-potato grower. Cassava is a drought-tolerant food-security staple consumed domestically; HS0714 exports are minimal. Production far exceeds trade.

AGO.note: FAOSTAT 2024: Angola is a top-10 cassava producer (~8-9 Mt); cassava is the dominant calorie source, eaten as funge and flour. Effectively no HS0714 trade — production vastly exceeds trade, a textbook eaten-where-grown staple.

EGY.note: FAOSTAT 2024: Egypt is a notable sweet-potato EXPORTER (HS071420) shipping to the Netherlands, UK, Saudi Arabia, France and Germany counter-seasonally. Small producer by global standards but a real net exporter of fresh sweet potato. (Cassava is not an Egyptian crop; this entry is sweet-potato-led.)

USA.note: USDA/FAOSTAT 2024: US output is sweet potato (~1.5 Mt, led by North Carolina/Mississippi/California) — a leading fresh sweet-potato EXPORTER to Canada, the Netherlands and the UK (HS071420). It also imports cassava (CHN, CRI) and yam/sweet-potato for ethnic markets. Roughly balanced root trade.

CRI.note: FAOSTAT 2024: Costa Rica is the leading Latin-American EXPORTER of fresh cassava (yuca) — to the US (CRI->USA ~110 kt) and the Netherlands (HS0714), wax-coated for the diaspora/retail market. Net cassava exporter.

NLD.note: FAOSTAT 2024: the Netherlands is the European re-export hub for tropical roots — importing fresh cassava and sweet potato from Egypt, Costa Rica, China, Ghana and the US (HS0714/071420), then re-exporting to Belgium, Germany and France. Net importer that redistributes across the EU.

rankings.note: Roots & tubers HS0714 (cassava fresh/dried + chips) plus HS071420 (sweet potato), 2024, kt. Export side is dominated by Thailand (#1 cassava exporter, ~60-65% of world cassava trade) with Vietnam, Cambodia and Laos behind it; import side by China (#1 cassava importer for feed/ethanol) and Thailand (which imports fresh roots to process and re-export). IMPORTANT: these rankings cover internationally traded roots only. The world's largest root producers — Nigeria, DR Congo, Ghana, Brazil, Indonesia — barely appear because their cassava/yam/sweet-potato output is eaten domestically. Global root production (~750+ Mt across cassava, sweet potato and yam) is roughly 20x the volume that crosses borders. Much of the East/SE-Asian starch trade also sits under HS1108 (tapioca starch), outside these HS0714 figures.

companies.name: Thai Wah PCL
companies.note: One of Thailand's largest cassava-starch and vermicelli producers (Rose Brand), with starch plants in Thailand, Cambodia and Vietnam supplying food, feed and industrial markets, mainly China. Listed on the SET. Buys fresh roots from Thai, Cambodian and Lao smallholders. 2024.
companies.improve: Reports group starch revenue but not fresh-root tonnage by origin; the smallholder/informal cross-border supply it relies on is invisible in HS0714 statistics.

companies.name: SPAC Starch (Sanguan Wongse / Eiamheng group)
companies.note: Major Thai native- and modified-tapioca-starch manufacturer (SPAC) in the Nakhon Ratchasima cassava belt, exporting starch to China and across Asia. 2024.
companies.improve: Private/closely held; capacity and origin-split sourcing are estimates, and most of its root intake comes through informal trader networks not captured in trade data.

companies.name: Vedan / Vietnam tapioca-starch processors
companies.note: Vietnam's cassava-starch sector (Vedan Vietnam and many provincial mills) exports ~2.4 Mt of cassava and products a year, ~93% to China. 2024.
companies.improve: Sector is highly fragmented across hundreds of mills; firm-level volumes and origin splits are not consistently published, and much fresh-root supply is smallholder/informal.

companies.name: Cargill
companies.note: Global agribusiness active in cassava/tapioca starch and starch sweeteners, trading and processing across Thailand, Vietnam and the Americas for food and industrial use. 2024.
companies.improve: Cassava-specific volumes are buried inside Cargill's starches & sweeteners segment; no public origin-split for roots.

companies.name: Ingredion
companies.note: Global ingredients firm producing tapioca/cassava starches and specialty modified starches from SE-Asian and South-American cassava for food and industrial customers. 2024.
companies.improve: Tapioca is one line within a broad starch portfolio; cassava sourcing tonnage by origin is not disclosed.

companies.name: Smallholder & informal cross-border traders
companies.note: HONEST FLAG: the bulk of the roots chain is NOT corporate. Tens of millions of smallholder farmers grow cassava/yam/sweet potato across SSA and the Mekong, and most cross-border fresh-cassava trade (Laos/Cambodia/Myanmar -> Thailand) moves through informal traders and border markets, not named companies. 2024.
companies.improve: This 'entity' is a placeholder for an unquantified informal sector; FoodShield cannot name or size these actors, and HS0714 trade statistics undercount this border trade.

global.note: World roots & tubers totals, kt (FAOSTAT 2024), covering cassava (~330-341 Mt), sweet potato (~90 Mt) and yam (~75 Mt); excludes potato (a separate FoodShield commodity). Africa grows ~65% of cassava and almost all the world's yam. Internationally traded roots (HS0714/071420) are only ~33-35 Mt — under 5% of production — because roots are bulky, perishable and overwhelmingly eaten where grown: a domestic food-security staple, not a globally traded commodity. The one big cross-border trade is cassava chips/pellets and starch feedstock from Thailand/Vietnam/Laos/Cambodia to China (much of the starch portion sits under HS1108, outside these figures).
